items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: We had Elvin Jones... So we have this opportunity to — and I got Elvin Jones... So we went from “Easy Living,” which is Michael Brecker and myself and cello... It’s very interesting.

ctx.x: Some of your best work do you think?

I measure my work by, did I do the very best that I could at the time. And this is definitely something that lives with me. I can play some of these charts and just go right back to stage and it’s the energy and the love and all, of making music together. And incidentally, as an aside, I just finished a CD which is a “Bobby Darin Homage” with Gary LeMel as the vocalist, president of Warner Brothers music, ex bass player, and Bobby Colomby of Blood Sweat and Tears is the producer and I’m the arranger. We had Elvin…

something at the mayor’s house in New York years and years ago for George Wein or some party. And he said, “I’d love to do it.” In fact the first thing he said to me, which is one of the dearest things that anybody’s ever said to me, we were hugging and he whispered in my ear, “Thad always talked about you.” And it was just like wow.
